title: 0. Fundamentals
summary: Start here: how computers and memory work, data structures and algorithms, how the web works (networking and hosting), and system design — high-level and low-level design.

title: 1. .NET
summary: The whole .NET ecosystem in learning order: C#, VB.NET and .NET internals (CLR, memory, GC); OOP, SOLID and patterns; ADO.NET, LINQ, Entity Framework and Dapper; Web Forms and MVC 5; ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API; exception handling, logging and custom controls; then architecture, clean code and microservices.

title: 2. Database, ETL & BI
summary: SQL Server and T-SQL from SELECT to tuning, SQL Server internals (storage, indexes, optimizer, transactions, locking), then ETL design, SSIS packages and SSRS reports.

title: 3. Cloud & DevOps
summary: Git first, then Docker and Kubernetes, Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines and the Azure services a .NET developer uses.

title: 4. Frontend
summary: HTML and CSS, JavaScript and TypeScript first, then jQuery, AngularJS (legacy), Angular, React and Vue.

title: 5. Automation & Industry 4.0
summary: Test automation with Selenium and Playwright, industrial automation (PLC, SCADA, Modbus, OPC UA) and Industry 4.0 (IIoT, MQTT, MES, OEE, digital twins).

title: 6. Web3 & Blockchain
summary: Blockchain fundamentals, Ethereum, wallets, Solidity smart contracts and dApp integration from .NET and JavaScript.

title: 7. Interview Questions & Career
summary: Role-based interview preparation (.NET full stack first), HR and behavioural rounds, team-lead rounds, career gaps, salary negotiation and company-wise preparation.
